242	/-! ## §2. Supplying the descent datum geometrically
243	
244	At schemes over an algebraically closed field the descent datum of §1 is not an
245	assumption: it follows from a section of `f^{(g)}` over a dense open of the Jacobian,
246	by the rational-map extension `extend_to_av` (Milne I.3.2, proved and unconditional)
247	packaged as `exists_unique_hom_restrict_eq_of_dense_open`. -/
248	
249	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
250	
251	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory MonObj
252	
253	variable {kbar : Type u} [Field kbar] [IsAlgClosed kbar]
254	
255	/-- **Milne's descent step, from birationality data.**
256	
257	Let `J` be an abelian variety over `k̄`, let `V ⊆ J` be a **dense open**, and let
258	`s : V ⟶ Sym^g C` be a section of `f^{(g)}` over `V` (i.e. `s ≫ f = V.ι`, which is
259	what birationality of `f^{(g)}` provides — Milne III.5.1(a)). Then for any
260	`h : Sym^g C ⟶ A` there is a unique `ψ : J ⟶ A` with `V.ι ≫ ψ = s ≫ h`.
261	
262	Existence and uniqueness are `exists_unique_hom_restrict_eq_of_dense_open`, i.e.
263	Milne Theorem I.3.2; the section is the only new input. This is the *only* step of
264	the Albanese proof that uses the rational-map extension, and its input is now
265	completely explicit. -/
266	theorem exists_unique_descent_of_section
267	    {J : Over (Spec (.of kbar))}
268	    [Smooth J.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible J.hom] [IsSeparated J.hom]
269	    [LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom] [IsIntegral J.left] [IsReduced J.left]
270	    {A : Over (Spec (.of kbar))}
271	    [GrpObj A] [IsProper A.hom] [Smooth A.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom]
272	    (V : J.left.Opens) (hV : Dense (V : Set J.left)) (k : (V : Scheme) ⟶ A.left)
273	    (hover : (Scheme.PartialMap.mk V hV k).toRationalMap.compHom A.hom
274	      = J.hom.toRationalMap) :
275	    ∃! ψ : J.left ⟶ A.left, V.ι ≫ ψ = k :=
276	  Scheme.RationalMap.exists_unique_hom_restrict_eq_of_dense_open V hV k hover
277	
278	/-- **A dense open inclusion is dominant.** Used to transport an equation proved on a
279	dense open to the whole (reduced) scheme. -/
280	theorem isDominant_opens_ι {X : Scheme.{u}} (V : X.Opens) (hV : Dense (V : Set X)) :
281	    IsDominant V.ι := by
282	  rw [isDominant_iff]
283	  simpa [DenseRange, Scheme.Opens.range_ι] using hV
284	
285	/-- **Milne's step 2 in full, from birationality data.**
286	
287	This is the descent datum `hdesc` of `exists_unique_albanese_factorisation`, produced
288	from exactly what Milne III.5.1(a) provides. Suppose `f : S ⟶ J` (morally
289	`f^{(g)} : Sym^g C ⟶ Pic⁰`) is an **isomorphism over a dense open** `V ⊆ J`, presented
290	concretely as
291	
292	* `s : V ⟶ S` with `s ≫ f = V.ι` — a section of `f` over `V`;
293	* `hsr` — and `s` is also a retraction of the restriction `f|_{f⁻¹V} : f⁻¹V ⟶ V`;
294	* `hVpre` — the preimage `f⁻¹V` is dense in `S`.
295	
296	Then for any `h : S ⟶ A` into an abelian variety there is a **unique** `ψ : J ⟶ A`
297	with `h = f ≫ ψ`.
298	
299	Note the shape of the conclusion: the equation is on **all** of `S`, not merely on
300	`V`. That is the difference between this and
301	`exists_unique_hom_restrict_eq_of_dense_open`, and it is where `hsr` and `hVpre` earn
302	their place — the extension theorem gives the equation on `V`, and agreement is then
303	transported to all of `S` along the dense open `f⁻¹V` (`ext_of_isDominant`, using that
304	`S` is reduced and `A` separated).
305	
306	So the Albanese descent needs no birational-inverse API. The full call-site bill is
307	**five** items, not four: the section `s`, the retraction `hsr`, the two density facts
308	`hV` and `hVpre`, and `hover` — the compatibility of the partial map with the structure
309	morphisms over `k̄`, which is what `exists_unique_hom_restrict_eq_of_dense_open`
310	(`Albanese/DenseOpenDescent.lean`) consumes. `hover` is a genuine hypothesis; it is
311	listed here because an earlier draft of this docstring omitted it. -/
312	theorem exists_unique_descent_of_birational
313	    {S J : Over (Spec (.of kbar))} [IsReduced S.left]
314	    [Smooth J.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible J.hom] [IsSeparated J.hom]
315	    [LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom] [IsIntegral J.left] [IsReduced J.left]
316	    {A : Over (Spec (.of kbar))}
317	    [GrpObj A] [IsProper A.hom] [Smooth A.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom]
318	    (f : S.left ⟶ J.left) (h : S.left ⟶ A.left)
319	    (V : J.left.Opens) (hV : Dense (V : Set J.left))
320	    (hVpre : Dense ((f ⁻¹ᵁ V : S.left.Opens) : Set S.left))
321	    (s : (V : Scheme) ⟶ S.left) (hs : s ≫ f = V.ι)
322	    (hsr : f.resLE V (f ⁻¹ᵁ V) le_rfl ≫ s = (f ⁻¹ᵁ V).ι)
323	    (hover : (Scheme.PartialMap.mk V hV (s ≫ h)).toRationalMap.compHom A.hom
324	      = J.hom.toRationalMap) :
325	    ∃! ψ : J.left ⟶ A.left, h = f ≫ ψ := by
326	  haveI : A.left.IsSeparated := Scheme.RationalMap.isSeparated_left_of_isProper A
327	  haveI hdom : IsDominant (f ⁻¹ᵁ V).ι := by
328	    rw [isDominant_iff]
329	    simpa [DenseRange, Scheme.Opens.range_ι] using hVpre
330	  obtain ⟨ψ, hψ, huniq⟩ :=
331	    Scheme.RationalMap.exists_unique_hom_restrict_eq_of_dense_open V hV (s ≫ h) hover
332	  refine ⟨ψ, ?_, ?_⟩
333	  · -- Both sides agree on the dense open `f⁻¹(V)`; transport to all of `S`.
334	    refine ext_of_isDominant (f ⁻¹ᵁ V).ι ?_
335	    calc (f ⁻¹ᵁ V).ι ≫ h
336	        = (f.resLE V (f ⁻¹ᵁ V) le_rfl ≫ s) ≫ h := by rw [hsr]
337	      _ = f.resLE V (f ⁻¹ᵁ V) le_rfl ≫ (s ≫ h) := by simp
338	      _ = f.resLE V (f ⁻¹ᵁ V) le_rfl ≫ (V.ι ≫ ψ) := by rw [hψ]
339	      _ = (f ⁻¹ᵁ V).ι ≫ f ≫ ψ := by
340	            rw [← Category.assoc,
341	              show f.resLE V (f ⁻¹ᵁ V) le_rfl ≫ V.ι = (f ⁻¹ᵁ V).ι ≫ f from by
342	                simp [Scheme.Hom.resLE], Category.assoc]
343	  · intro ψ' hψ'
344	    refine huniq ψ' ?_
345	    change V.ι ≫ ψ' = s ≫ h
346	    rw [← hs, Category.assoc, ← hψ']
347	
348	/-! ### Crossing from scheme morphisms to `Over (Spec k̄)` morphisms
349	
350	`exists_unique_descent_of_birational` concludes about `J.left ⟶ A.left`, whereas the
351	connector of §1 lives in `Over (Spec k̄)`. The two lemmas below cross that gap, and the
352	crossing is free rather than an extra hypothesis: compatibility with the structure
353	morphisms is *automatic* once `f` is dominant. -/
354	
355	omit [IsAlgClosed kbar] in
356	/-- **Compatibility over `k̄` is automatic.** If `f : S ⟶ J` has dominant underlying
357	morphism and `ψ` satisfies `h.left = f.left ≫ ψ`, then `ψ` is a morphism over `k̄`:
358	`ψ ≫ A.hom = J.hom`.
359	
360	Both sides agree after the dominant `f.left` (each reduces to the structure morphism of
361	`S`, by `h.w` and `f.w`), and `J.left` is reduced, so `ext_of_isDominant` concludes.
362	This is why the descent produces an honest `Over` morphism without assuming it. -/
363	theorem comp_hom_of_descent_eq
364	    {S J A : Over (Spec (.of kbar))} [IsReduced J.left]
365	    (f : S ⟶ J) (h : S ⟶ A) (ψ : J.left ⟶ A.left)
366	    (hfd : IsDominant f.left) (hψ : h.left = f.left ≫ ψ) :
367	    ψ ≫ A.hom = J.hom := by
368	  refine ext_of_isDominant f.left ?_
369	  rw [← Category.assoc, ← hψ]
370	  exact h.w.trans f.w.symm
371	
372	omit [IsAlgClosed kbar] in
373	/-- **Transport the descent datum into `Over (Spec k̄)`.** A unique factorisation of
374	underlying scheme morphisms upgrades to a unique factorisation of `k̄`-morphisms, using
375	`comp_hom_of_descent_eq` for the structure-map compatibility.
376	
377	This delivers `hdesc` in exactly the shape `exists_unique_albanese_factorisation`
378	consumes. -/
379	theorem exists_unique_descent_over
380	    {S J A : Over (Spec (.of kbar))} [IsReduced J.left]
381	    (f : S ⟶ J) (h : S ⟶ A) (hfd : IsDominant f.left)
382	    (hyp : ∃! ψ : J.left ⟶ A.left, h.left = f.left ≫ ψ) :
383	    ∃! ψ : J ⟶ A, h = f ≫ ψ := by
384	  obtain ⟨ψ, hψ, huniq⟩ := hyp
385	  refine ⟨Over.homMk ψ (comp_hom_of_descent_eq f h ψ hfd hψ),
386	    Over.OverMorphism.ext (by simpa using hψ), ?_⟩
387	  intro ψ' hψ'
388	  refine Over.OverMorphism.ext ?_
389	  exact huniq ψ'.left (by simpa using congrArg Over.Hom.left (a₁ := h) hψ')
390	
391	omit [IsAlgClosed kbar] in
392	/-- **Uniqueness of the Albanese descent, geometrically.** Two morphisms from the
393	Jacobian to an abelian variety that agree on a dense open are equal — the
394	reduced-and-separated agreement principle, in the form the descent uses. -/
395	theorem hom_ext_of_dense_open
396	    {J : Over (Spec (.of kbar))} [IsReduced J.left]
397	    {A : Over (Spec (.of kbar))} [IsProper A.hom]
398	    (V : J.left.Opens) (hV : Dense (V : Set J.left))
399	    {ψ₁ ψ₂ : J.left ⟶ A.left} (h : V.ι ≫ ψ₁ = V.ι ≫ ψ₂) : ψ₁ = ψ₂ := by
400	  haveI : A.left.IsSeparated := Scheme.RationalMap.isSeparated_left_of_isProper A
401	  haveI := isDominant_opens_ι V hV
402	  exact ext_of_isDominant V.ι h

404	/-! ## §3. End to end: `SymPowData` + birationality ⟹ the Albanese universal property
405	
406	The capstone. Everything above is assembled into one statement whose hypotheses are
407	**only** the two things this leg genuinely owes:
408	
409	1. `D : SymPowData C g` — the symmetric power with its universal property;
410	2. Milne III.5.1(a) birationality of `f^{(g)}`, in the concrete form of a section `s`
411	   over a dense open `V`, a matching retraction, dominance, and two density facts.
412	
413	No `sorry`-bodied object appears, no rational-map reasoning is left at the call site,
414	and the result is axiom-clean.
415	
416	**Stated precisely, so "finished" is not read too generously.** What is proved is the
417	*implication*: given (1) and (2), Milne III.6.1 holds. Every step of his argument is
418	machine-checked, and no step of it is what remains. But the antecedent is currently
419	witnessed only for `g = 1` (`symPowDataOne` with `symPowDataOne_proj_perm`), which is
420	the case where the group-law step degenerates — see the warning in
421	`Albanese/SymPowInterface.lean`. So this is a complete argument awaiting a
422	construction, not a theorem about the actual `Sym^g C`. -/
423	
424	/-- **Milne Proposition III.6.1, end to end.**
425	
426	From the symmetric-power interface and Milne III.5.1(a)'s birationality data alone, a
427	pointed `φ : C ⟶ A` into an abelian variety factors uniquely through the pointed
428	`aj : C ⟶ J` whose symmetrisation is `f`:
429	
430	`∃! ψ : J ⟶ A, φ = aj ≫ ψ`.
431	
432	**Axiom-clean** (`[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`). The chain is
433	`exists_unique_descent_of_birational` → `exists_unique_descent_over` →
434	`exists_unique_albanese_factorisation`, with commutativity and pointed rigidity
435	supplied by `Albanese/AVSelfProduct.lean`.
436	
437	Note that no curve hypothesis appears: `g` is just the number of factors. -/
438	theorem exists_unique_albanese_factorisation_of_birational
439	    {C : Over (Spec (.of kbar))} {g : ℕ}
440	    (D : SymPowData C g)
441	    (hproj : ∀ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin g), permAut C σ ≫ D.proj = D.proj)
442	    (P0 : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of kbar))) ⟶ C) (i₀ : Fin g)
443	    {J A : Over (Spec (.of kbar))}
444	    [GrpObj J] [IsProper J.hom] [Smooth J.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible J.hom]
445	    [IsIntegral J.left] [IsReduced J.left]
446	    [GrpObj A] [IsProper A.hom] [Smooth A.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom]
447	    [IsReduced (D.carrier).left]
448	    (φ : C ⟶ A) (hφ : P0 ≫ φ = η[A])
449	    (aj : C ⟶ J) (f : D.carrier ⟶ J)
450	    (hf : letI : IsCommMonObj J := isCommMonObj_of_isProper_smooth_of_package J
451	      D.proj ≫ f = powSum g aj)
452	    (haj0 : P0 ≫ aj = η[J])
453	    (hfd : IsDominant f.left)
454	    (V : J.left.Opens) (hV : Dense (V : Set J.left))
455	    (hVpre : Dense ((f.left ⁻¹ᵁ V : (D.carrier).left.Opens) : Set (D.carrier).left))
456	    (s : (V : Scheme) ⟶ (D.carrier).left) (hs : s ≫ f.left = V.ι)
457	    (hsr : f.left.resLE V (f.left ⁻¹ᵁ V) le_rfl ≫ s = (f.left ⁻¹ᵁ V).ι)
458	    (hover : letI : IsCommMonObj A := isCommMonObj_of_isProper_smooth_of_package A
459	      (Scheme.PartialMap.mk V hV (s ≫ (D.symAVMap φ).left)).toRationalMap.compHom A.hom
460	        = J.hom.toRationalMap) :
461	    ∃! ψ : J ⟶ A, φ = aj ≫ ψ := by
462	  letI : IsCommMonObj J := isCommMonObj_of_isProper_smooth_of_package J
463	  letI : IsCommMonObj A := isCommMonObj_of_isProper_smooth_of_package A
464	  refine exists_unique_albanese_factorisation D f P0 i₀ hproj aj hf haj0 φ hφ
465	    (fun ψ hψ => isMonHom_of_pointed ψ hψ) ?_
466	  exact exists_unique_descent_over f (D.symAVMap φ) hfd
467	    (exists_unique_descent_of_birational f.left (D.symAVMap φ).left V hV hVpre s hs hsr hover)

variable (A B B' : Type*) [CommSemiring A] [Ring B] [Semiring B'] [Algebra A B] [Algebra A B']
variable (G : Type*) [Monoid G] [MulSemiringAction G B] [SMulCommClass G A B]

/-- The set of fixed points under a group action, as a subring. -/
def FixedPoints.subsemiring : Subsemiring B' where
  __ := FixedPoints.addSubmonoid G B'
  __ := FixedPoints.submonoid G B'

def FixedPoints.subring : Subring B where
  __ := FixedPoints.addSubgroup G B
  __ := FixedPoints.submonoid G B

instance : SMulCommClass G (FixedPoints.subring B G) B :=
  inferInstanceAs (SMulCommClass G (FixedPoints.subsemiring B G) B)

/-- The set of fixed points under a group action, as a subalgebra. -/
def FixedPoints.subalgebra : Subalgebra A B' where
  __ := FixedPoints.subsemiring B' G
  algebraMap_mem' r g := smul_algebraMap g r

instance : SMulCommClass G (FixedPoints.subalgebra A B' G) B' :=
  inferInstanceAs (SMulCommClass G (FixedPoints.subsemiring B' G) B')

module

public import Mathlib.RingTheory.Invariant.Defs
public import Mathlib.RingTheory.IntegralClosure.IntegralRestrict
public import Mathlib.RingTheory.LocalRing.ResidueField.Ideal

/-!
# Invariant Extensions of Rings

Given an extension of rings `B/A` and an action of `G` on `B`, we introduce a predicate
`Algebra.IsInvariant A B G` which states that every fixed point of `B` lies in the image of `A`.

The main application is in algebraic number theory, where `G := Gal(L/K)` is the Galois group
of some finite Galois extension of number fields, and `A := 𝓞K` and `B := 𝓞L` are their ring of
integers. This main result in this file implies the existence of Frobenius elements in this setting.
See `Mathlib/RingTheory/Frobenius.lean`.

## Main statements

Let `G` be a finite group acting on a commutative ring `B` satisfying `Algebra.IsInvariant A B G`.

* `Algebra.IsInvariant.isIntegral`: `B/A` is an integral extension.
* `Algebra.IsInvariant.exists_smul_of_under_eq`: `G` acts transitivity on the prime ideals of `B`
  lying above a given prime ideal of `A`.

If `Q` is a prime ideal of `B` lying over a prime ideal `P` of `A`, then

* `IsFractionRing.stabilizerHom_surjective`:
  The stabilizer subgroup of `Q` surjects onto `Aut(Frac(B/Q)/Frac(A/P))`.
* `Ideal.Quotient.stabilizerHom_surjective`:
  The stabilizer subgroup of `Q` surjects onto `Aut((B/Q)/(A/P))`.
* `Ideal.Quotient.exists_algEquiv_fixedPoint_quotient_under`:
  If `k` is a domain containing `B/Q`, then any `A/P`-algebra automorphism of `k` restricts to
  an automorphism of `B/Q`.
-/

@[expose] public section

open scoped Pointwise

section Galois

variable (A K L B : Type*) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Field K] [Field L]
  [Algebra A K] [Algebra B L] [IsFractionRing A K] [IsFractionRing B L]
  [Algebra A B] [Algebra K L] [Algebra A L] [IsScalarTower A K L] [IsScalarTower A B L]
  [IsIntegrallyClosed A] [IsIntegralClosure B A L]

/-- In the AKLB setup, the Galois group of `L/K` acts on `B`. -/
@[implicit_reducible]
noncomputable def IsIntegralClosure.MulSemiringAction [Algebra.IsAlgebraic K L] :
    MulSemiringAction Gal(L/K) B :=
  MulSemiringAction.compHom B (galRestrict A K L B).toMonoidHom

instance [Algebra.IsAlgebraic K L] : let := IsIntegralClosure.MulSemiringAction A K L B
    SMulDistribClass Gal(L/K) B L :=
  let := IsIntegralClosure.MulSemiringAction A K L B
  ⟨fun g b l ↦ by
    simp only [Algebra.smul_def, smul_mul', mul_eq_mul_right_iff]
    exact Or.inl (algebraMap_galRestrictHom_apply A K L B g b).symm⟩

/-- In the AKLB setup, every fixed point of `B` lies in the image of `A`. -/
theorem Algebra.isInvariant_of_isGalois [FiniteDimensional K L] [h : IsGalois K L] :
    letI := IsIntegralClosure.MulSemiringAction A K L B
    Algebra.IsInvariant A B Gal(L/K) := by
  replace h := ((IsGalois.tfae (F := K) (E := L)).out 0 1).mp h
  letI := IsIntegralClosure.MulSemiringAction A K L B
  refine ⟨fun b hb ↦ ?_⟩
  replace hb : algebraMap B L b ∈ IntermediateField.fixedField (⊤ : Subgroup Gal(L/K)) := by
    rintro ⟨g, -⟩
    exact (algebraMap_galRestrict_apply A g b).symm.trans (congrArg (algebraMap B L) (hb g))
  rw [h, IntermediateField.mem_bot] at hb
  obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := hb
  have hb : IsIntegral A b := IsIntegralClosure.isIntegral A L b
  rw [← isIntegral_algebraMap_iff (FaithfulSMul.algebraMap_injective B L), ← hk,
    isIntegral_algebraMap_iff (FaithfulSMul.algebraMap_injective K L)] at hb

`exists_unique_descent_of_birational` → `exists_unique_descent_over` →
`exists_unique_albanese_factorisation`, with commutativity and pointed rigidity
supplied by `Albanese/AVSelfProduct.lean`.

Note that no curve hypothesis appears: `g` is just the number of factors. -/
theorem exists_unique_albanese_factorisation_of_birational
    {C : Over (Spec (.of kbar))} {g : ℕ}
    (D : SymPowData C g)
    (hproj : ∀ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin g), permAut C σ ≫ D.proj = D.proj)
    (P0 : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of kbar))) ⟶ C) (i₀ : Fin g)
    {J A : Over (Spec (.of kbar))}
    [GrpObj J] [IsProper J.hom] [Smooth J.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible J.hom]
    [IsIntegral J.left] [IsReduced J.left]
    [GrpObj A] [IsProper A.hom] [Smooth A.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom]
    [IsReduced (D.carrier).left]
    (φ : C ⟶ A) (hφ : P0 ≫ φ = η[A])
    (aj : C ⟶ J) (f : D.carrier ⟶ J)
    (hf : letI : IsCommMonObj J := isCommMonObj_of_isProper_smooth_of_package J
      D.proj ≫ f = powSum g aj)
    (haj0 : P0 ≫ aj = η[J])
    (hfd : IsDominant f.left)
    (V : J.left.Opens) (hV : Dense (V : Set J.left))
    (hVpre : Dense ((f.left ⁻¹ᵁ V : (D.carrier).left.Opens) : Set (D.carrier).left))
    (s : (V : Scheme) ⟶ (D.carrier).left) (hs : s ≫ f.left = V.ι)
    (hsr : f.left.resLE V (f.left ⁻¹ᵁ V) le_rfl ≫ s = (f.left ⁻¹ᵁ V).ι)
    (hover : letI : IsCommMonObj A := isCommMonObj_of_isProper_smooth_of_package A
      (Scheme.PartialMap.mk V hV (s ≫ (D.symAVMap φ).left)).toRationalMap.compHom A.hom
        = J.hom.toRationalMap) :
    ∃! ψ : J ⟶ A, φ = aj ≫ ψ := by
  letI : IsCommMonObj J := isCommMonObj_of_isProper_smooth_of_package J
  letI : IsCommMonObj A := isCommMonObj_of_isProper_smooth_of_package A
  refine exists_unique_albanese_factorisation D f P0 i₀ hproj aj hf haj0 φ hφ
    (fun ψ hψ => isMonHom_of_pointed ψ hψ) ?_
  exact exists_unique_descent_over f (D.symAVMap φ) hfd
    (exists_unique_descent_of_birational f.left (D.symAVMap φ).left V hV hVpre s hs hsr hover)

end AlgebraicGeometry

6	import Mathlib
7	
8	/-!
9	# The `g`-fold sum `C^g ⟶ A` and its permutation symmetry
10	
11	Milne's proof of the Albanese universal property (*Abelian Varieties* III.6
12	Proposition 6.1) opens with "clearly this is symmetric, and so it factors
13	through `C^{(g)}`", where "this" is
14	
15	`C^g ⟶ A`,  `(P₁, …, P_g) ↦ φ(P₁) + ⋯ + φ(P_g)`
16	
17	for `φ : C ⟶ A` a morphism into an abelian variety. This file supplies that
18	morphism together with the content behind the word "clearly": its invariance
19	under permuting the `g` factors. It is the input that the universal property of
20	the symmetric power `Sym^g C` consumes.
21	
22	## The mechanism: hom-sets into a group object are commutative monoids
23	
24	The whole file rests on a Mathlib fact that makes the geometry evaporate. In a
25	cartesian monoidal category, `Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Cartesian/Mon.lean`
26	equips the hom-set `X ⟶ A` of a monoid object `A` with a `Monoid` structure
27	whose multiplication is *definitionally* `f * h = lift f h ≫ μ[A]`, and upgrades
28	it to a `CommMonoid` when `A` is a commutative monoid object (`IsCommMonObj`).
29	`Over (Spec k̄)` is cartesian monoidal and braided, and an abelian variety is a
30	commutative group object there.
31	
32	So the `g`-fold sum is a `Finset.prod` of morphisms, its symmetry is
33	`Equiv.prod_comp`, and no hand-rolled induction over `Fin g` is needed. Stating
34	it this way is not a shortcut: it is the correct observation that Milne's
35	"clearly" is exactly the commutativity of `A`'s group law and nothing else.
36	
37	## Main definitions
38	
39	* `MonObj.preHom` — precomposition `(X ⟶ A) →* (W ⟶ A)` as a monoid
40	  homomorphism. Mathlib gives the hom-set its monoid structure but does not
41	  record that precomposition respects it; this is what lets `map_prod` move a
42	  precomposition through the products below.
43	* `MonObj.permAut` — the automorphism of `∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n => C)` permuting the
44	  factors along `σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)`.
45	* `MonObj.powSum` — the morphism `∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n => C) ⟶ A` sending
46	  `(P₁, …, P_n) ↦ φ(P₁) * ⋯ * φ(P_n)`, i.e. the product over `i : Fin n` of the
47	  projections composed with `φ`.
48	
49	## Main results
50	
51	* `MonObj.powSum_perm` — **`powSum` is `S_n`-symmetric**:
52	  `permAut C σ ≫ powSum n φ = powSum n φ`. This is Milne's "clearly this is
53	  symmetric", and the hypothesis the symmetric-power universal property consumes.
54	* `MonObj.comp_powSum` — `powSum` is natural in the source.
55	
56	## Instantiating this at an abelian variety
57	
58	`powSum` requires `[IsCommMonObj A]`, which is *load-bearing*: without it the
59	hom-set is only a `Monoid`, the `∏` notation cannot be written, and the symmetry
60	is false. It is **not** obtained by synthesis, but it *is* available as a theorem on
61	the project's standard abelian-variety package — use
62	
63	```
64	letI := isCommMonObj_of_isProper_smooth_of_package A
65	```
66	
67	(`AlgebraicGeometry.isCommMonObj_of_isProper_smooth_of_package`,
68	`Albanese/AVSelfProduct.lean`: Milne §I.1 Corollary 1.4, proved from the Rigidity
69	Lemma, with the three `A ⊗ A` side conditions discharged).
70	
71	Earlier revisions of this note said the project *could not* supply `IsCommMonObj`,
72	because `isCommMonObj_of_isProper_smooth` (`Albanese/AVCommutative.lean`) carries
73	hypotheses `[GeometricallyIrreducible (A ⊗ A).hom] [LocallyOfFiniteType (A ⊗ A).hom]
74	[IsReduced (A ⊗ A).left]` that synthesis cannot discharge. That was a statement about
75	instance **keying**, not about the mathematics: `(A ⊗ A).hom` is reducibly
76	`pullback.fst A.hom A.hom ≫ A.hom` (`Over.tensorObj_hom`), and one rewrite puts each
77	goal in a form mathlib's own instances solve. See `Albanese/AVSelfProduct.lean`.
78	
79	## Scope
80	
81	This file deliberately stops at the symmetry statement. It does **not** construct
82	`Sym^n C`: at this Mathlib pin there is no quotient of a scheme by a finite group
83	action (see `analogies/m3-route-audit.md`, which scopes that construction at
84	roughly 2400–3800 lines). What is supplied here is the *input* to the symmetric
85	power's universal property, which is the half of Milne's symmetrisation step that
86	does not depend on the quotient existing.
87	
88	The other half now has a home: `Albanese/SymPowInterface.lean` takes that universal
89	property as **data** (`SymPowData`) and uses `powSum_perm` below to turn Milne's
90	`Sym^n φ` into a construction. The quotient is still missing as an *object*, but no
91	statement downstream of it is a statement about a `sorry` any more.
92	
93	## References
94	
95	Milne, *Abelian Varieties*, §III.6 Proposition 6.1, p. 104; blueprint
96	`lem:symmetric_product_av_map` in
97	`blueprint/src/chapters/Albanese_AlbaneseUP.tex`.
98	-/
99	
100	set_option autoImplicit false
101	
102	universe v u
103	
104	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
105	
106	namespace CategoryTheory.MonObj
107	
108	variable {K : Type u} [Category.{v} K] [CartesianMonoidalCategory K]
109	
110	/-! ## §0. Precomposition is a monoid homomorphism on hom-sets
111	
112	`Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Cartesian/Mon.lean` gives `X ⟶ A` its monoid
113	structure with `f * h = lift f h ≫ μ[A]` and `1 = toUnit X ≫ η[A]`, but does not
114	record that *precomposition* respects it. It does, and bundling it as a
115	`MonoidHom` is what lets `map_prod` move a precomposition through the finite
116	products below. -/
117	
118	/-- **Precomposition with `u : W ⟶ X`, as a monoid homomorphism**
119	`(X ⟶ A) →* (W ⟶ A)`. Multiplicativity is `comp_lift` (a lift precomposed is the
120	lift of the precompositions); unitality is uniqueness of the map to the unit
121	object. -/
122	noncomputable def preHom {A X W : K} [MonObj A] (u : W ⟶ X) : (X ⟶ A) →* (W ⟶ A) where
123	  toFun f := u ≫ f
124	  map_one' := by
125	    change u ≫ (toUnit X ≫ η[A]) = toUnit W ≫ η[A]
126	    rw [← Category.assoc]
127	    congr 1
128	    exact Subsingleton.elim _ _
129	  map_mul' f h := by
130	    change u ≫ (lift f h ≫ μ[A]) = lift (u ≫ f) (u ≫ h) ≫ μ[A]
131	    rw [← Category.assoc, comp_lift]
132	
133	@[simp]
134	theorem preHom_apply {A X W : K} [MonObj A] (u : W ⟶ X) (f : X ⟶ A) :
135	    preHom u f = u ≫ f := rfl
136	
137	section PermAut
138	
139	variable [HasFiniteProducts K]
140	
141	/-- **The factor-permuting automorphism of `C^n`.** For `σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)`,
142	the morphism `C^n ⟶ C^n` whose `i`-th component is the `σ i`-th projection; on
143	points, `(P₁, …, P_n) ↦ (P_{σ 1}, …, P_{σ n})`. -/
144	noncomputable def permAut (C : K) {n : ℕ} (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) :
145	    (∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n => C)) ⟶ (∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n => C)) :=
146	  Pi.lift (fun i => Pi.π (fun _ : Fin n => C) (σ i))
147	
148	omit [CartesianMonoidalCategory K] in
149	@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
150	theorem permAut_π (C : K) {n : ℕ} (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (i : Fin n) :
151	    permAut C σ ≫ Pi.π (fun _ : Fin n => C) i = Pi.π (fun _ : Fin n => C) (σ i) := by
152	  simp only [permAut, Pi.lift_π]
153	
154	end PermAut
155	
156	section PowSum
157	
158	variable [HasFiniteProducts K] [BraidedCategory K]
159	
160	/-- **The `n`-fold sum morphism `C^n ⟶ A`.** For `φ : C ⟶ A` into a commutative
161	group object, the morphism sending `(P₁, …, P_n) ↦ φ(P₁) * ⋯ * φ(P_n)`, formed as
162	the product in the commutative monoid `(C^n ⟶ A)` of the projections composed
163	with `φ`.
164	
165	In the Albanese application `A` is an abelian variety and the group law is
166	written additively: this is `(P₁, …, P_g) ↦ φ(P₁) + ⋯ + φ(P_g)`. -/
167	noncomputable def powSum {C A : K} [MonObj A] [IsCommMonObj A] (n : ℕ) (φ : C ⟶ A) :
168	    (∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n => C)) ⟶ A :=
169	  ∏ i, (Pi.π (fun _ : Fin n => C) i ≫ φ)
170	
171	/-- **Milne's "clearly this is symmetric".** The `n`-fold sum is invariant under
172	permuting the factors of `C^n`. The proof is exactly the commutativity of the
173	group law of `A`: in the *commutative* monoid `(C^n ⟶ A)` a finite product is
174	invariant under reindexing (`Equiv.prod_comp`).
175	
176	This is the hypothesis consumed by the universal property of the symmetric power
177	`Sym^n C`, which is what licenses the factorisation `C^n ⟶ Sym^n C ⟶ A`. -/
178	theorem powSum_perm {C A : K} [MonObj A] [IsCommMonObj A] (n : ℕ) (φ : C ⟶ A)
179	    (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) :
180	    permAut C σ ≫ powSum n φ = powSum n φ := by
181	  classical
182	  calc permAut C σ ≫ powSum n φ
183	      = ∏ i, (permAut C σ ≫ Pi.π (fun _ : Fin n => C) i ≫ φ) :=
184	        map_prod (preHom (permAut C σ)) _ Finset.univ
185	    _ = ∏ i, (Pi.π (fun _ : Fin n => C) (σ i) ≫ φ) :=
186	        Finset.prod_congr rfl fun i _ => by rw [← Category.assoc, permAut_π]
187	    _ = ∏ i, (Pi.π (fun _ : Fin n => C) i ≫ φ) :=
188	        Equiv.prod_comp σ (fun i => Pi.π (fun _ : Fin n => C) i ≫ φ)
189	
190	/-- `powSum` is natural in the source: precomposition distributes over the sum. -/
191	theorem comp_powSum {C A W : K} [MonObj A] [IsCommMonObj A] (n : ℕ) (φ : C ⟶ A)
192	    (u : W ⟶ (∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n => C))) :
193	    u ≫ powSum n φ = ∏ i, (u ≫ Pi.π (fun _ : Fin n => C) i ≫ φ) := by
194	  classical
195	  exact map_prod (preHom u) _ Finset.univ
196	
197	end PowSum
198	
199	end CategoryTheory.MonObj

module

public import Mathlib.Algebra.Algebra.Defs

/-!
# Invariant Extensions of Rings

Given an extension of rings `B/A` and an action of `G` on `B`, we introduce a predicate
`Algebra.IsInvariant A B G` which states that every fixed point of `B` lies in the image of `A`.

The main application is in algebraic number theory, where `G := Gal(L/K)` is the Galois group
of some finite Galois extension of number fields, and `A := 𝓞K` and `B := 𝓞L` are their rings of
integers.
-/

public section

namespace Algebra

variable (A B G : Type*) [CommSemiring A] [Semiring B] [Algebra A B]
  [Group G] [MulSemiringAction G B]

/-- An action of a group `G` on an extension of rings `B/A` is invariant if every fixed point of
`B` lies in the image of `A`. The converse statement that every point in the image of `A` is fixed
by `G` is `smul_algebraMap` (assuming `SMulCommClass A B G`). -/
@[mk_iff] class IsInvariant : Prop where
  isInvariant : ∀ b : B, (∀ g : G, g • b = b) → ∃ a : A, algebraMap A B a = b

end Algebra

import Mathlib

set_option autoImplicit false
universe v u
open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory

variable {K : Type u} [Category.{v} K] [CartesianMonoidalCategory K] [HasFiniteProducts K]

noncomputable def permAut (C : K) {n : ℕ} (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) :
    (∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n => C)) ⟶ (∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n => C)) :=
  Pi.lift (fun i => Pi.π (fun _ : Fin n => C) (σ i))

structure SymPowData (C : K) (n : ℕ) where
  carrier : K
  proj : (∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n => C)) ⟶ carrier
  desc : ∀ {T : K} (h : (∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n => C)) ⟶ T),
    (∀ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n), permAut C σ ≫ h = h) →
    ∃! u : carrier ⟶ T, proj ≫ u = h

/-- Sym^n(point) = point, for every n. -/
noncomputable def symPowDataUnit (n : ℕ) : SymPowData (𝟙_ K) n where
  carrier := 𝟙_ K
  proj := toUnit _
  desc := fun {T} h _ => by
    have hret : (toUnit (∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin n => (𝟙_ K)))) ≫ Pi.lift (fun _ : Fin n => 𝟙 (𝟙_ K))
        = 𝟙 _ := by
      apply Pi.hom_ext
      intro b

example (R A : Type) [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [Algebra R A] (n : ℕ) (e : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) :
    (⨂[R] _ : Fin n, A) ≃ₐ[R] (⨂[R] _ : Fin n, A) := by
  exact? says exact AlgEquiv.refl

import Mathlib

open scoped TensorProduct
open PiTensorProduct

-- Can we upgrade the linear `reindex` to an algebra automorphism of the n-fold tensor power?
noncomputable def permAlg (R A : Type) [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [Algebra R A] (n : ℕ)
    (e : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) : (⨂[R] _ : Fin n, A) →ₐ[R] (⨂[R] _ : Fin n, A) := by
  classical
  exact
    { toFun := PiTensorProduct.reindex R (fun _ : Fin n => A) e
      map_one' := by simp [PiTensorProduct.one_def]
      map_mul' := by
        intro x y
        induction x using PiTensorProduct.induction_on with
        | smul_tprod r a =>

        | add hx hx' => simp [add_mul, hx, hx']
      map_zero' := by simp
      map_add' := by simp
      commutes' := by
        intro r
        simp [Algebra.algebraMap_eq_smul_one, PiTensorProduct.one_def] }

    (e : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) : (⨂[R] _ : Fin n, A) →ₐ[R] (⨂[R] _ : Fin n, A) := by
